outcome.answer:
You generally can’t deterministically guess the number of tokens an AI will generate from the prompt alone, because output length varies with a prompt-conditioned output-length distribution that can be heavy-tailed rather than a single scalar target. Robust length prediction therefore needs to treat multiple generations from the same prompt as evidence of that distribution (e.g., via prompt-conditioned methods). [4]

If the model (or an agent) can internally estimate how much response remains, you may get more consistent length structure: evidence suggests total response length can be linearly decodable from the prompt’s last hidden state, and the model also shows measurable shifts when it retracts and restarts a partial solution. [1]

For token usage during agent execution, length can vary by over an order of magnitude across runs because tool feedback and context growth change future inputs; methods like TokenCast forecast using composable cost across execution segments and refresh the forecast as new evidence arrives. [5]

(These differ in whether they target pure completion-length forecasting [4,1] versus end-to-end agent token consumption under evolving context [5].)
